messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Roadmap of RHipe
parts:
Hi,

So, there isn't too much to extend.

a) A protocol buffer based sequence file format, so it can be read
from other languages.
b) better debugging support
c) Maybe extra addons e.g. regression on RHIPE, see
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE-Additions
d) improvements to reducer when millions of keys each with a few set
of values (in this cass more time is spent on parsing/setting up
context for the expression than any useful work)
e) tutorials/papers.
f) Possibly, automatically ave the calling environment, so that the
map/reducer code automatically can access the functions declared
outside (only persist objects less than X bytes large or place a cap
on total size of persisted objects)

Do you or anybody else have suggestions for improvements?

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: Re: Roadmap of RHipe
parts:
Rhipe is feeling quite mature. This list looks good. Is "submit to
CRAN" on the list?

For (f), what would be nice would be the ability to automatically
parse the map and reduce to see which objects in the calling
environment are used and automatically share them, if that is
possible. I think foreach does something like this.

Also, maybe this already exists, but it would be nice to have an
option for rhipe to not kill the entire job when there is stderr
output for any one task but instead collect these and tell them to the
user at the end of the job, and set the key and values for the bad
tasks to something that indicates this.

messages.subject: Re: Roadmap of RHipe
parts:
Yes, but the more I think about it the more it is probably just a
special case. I am reading in ~200K data files from another binary
format and about 3 or 4 are bad data files that throw an error. I
would not discover these until very late in the process. try() and
suppressMessages() didn't help because I was calling external code
which would still emit stderr stuff regardless of what I did. The
final workaround was to modify the external code. But again, this is
a special case - was just on my mind when I replied.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Roadmap of RHipe
parts:
So in R, and correct me if i'm wrong, the warning and error functions
are sent through
Re_WriteConsoleEx . So i can't differentiate a warning from an error.

Now the Java code receives this and throws an exception to kill the job.

My plan is this: for a debug mode

1. Errors return the map.input.file and block which has been sent to them.
2. These are are stored in a separate file.
3. RHIPE functions (say in R console) to read these blocks (in a
stream) for local in console debugging.
4. Optionally, during other uses, skip first N errors.

Does it sound okay?
Regards
Saptarshi
